options.text: Water vapour in the air touches the cold box and changes into liquid droplets by condensation.
Water vapour in the air turns into liquid droplets by evaporation.
The lunch box becomes cold because water vapour turns into droplets on it.
Water leaks from inside the lunch box through the steel wall.

stem:
Tanya takes a chilled steel lunch box out of the fridge on a humid morning. Small water droplets soon form on the outside of the box.

Where do those outside droplets come from?

teacher.key_rationale: Outside droplets form when water vapour in the air meets a cold surface and condenses. Evaporation is the opposite change; the cold box causes condensation, and steel walls do not leak vapour that way.
